title: Minimum Swaps to Move Zeros to End
summary: Given an integer array nums, determine the minimum number of operations required to move all zeros to the end of the array.
statement: Given an integer array nums, determine the minimum number of operations required to move all zeros to the end of the array. In one operation, you can swap any two distinct elements nums[i] and nums[j].
constraints: One operation swaps any two distinct positions.
Move every zero into a suffix of the array.
Return the minimum number of swaps; relative order need not be preserved.
hints: The final suffix has length equal to the zero count.
Each zero before that suffix is misplaced.
One arbitrary swap pairs one misplaced zero with one misplaced nonzero.
Thus the misplaced-zero count is both necessary and sufficient.
editorial: Thus the misplaced-zero count is both necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: Two zeros occupy the first three positions, so two swaps move them behind all nonzeros.
Zeros already form the suffix, so no swap is needed.
